LFP Compression: Decoding-Aware Tuning

electrophysiology
LFP
compression
Neuropixels
decoding
Does lossy LFP compression degrade downstream decoding of behaviour, and what should we ship instead of the current aggressive tier? Wheel speed, choice and feedback decoded across 11 benchmark recordings under three compression sweeps.
Author

Olivier Winter

Published

August 31, 2026

Overview

The SVD/WP compression benchmark calibrates ε and α against RMSE and SNR — a spatial/amplitude fidelity proxy that says nothing about whether the information downstream analyses use survives compression. This page checks that directly, by decoding wheel speed, choice and feedback from LFP band-power envelopes across the 11 benchmark recordings, then uses the result to search for a better operating point than the current two-tier design.

lfpack’s codec is two independent stages, applied in sequence (compress() in packages/lfpack/src/lfpack/_core.py):

  1. SVD stage — ε only. Rank r = #{k : sv[k] > ε·σ₀} is fixed from the raw singular-value spectrum before α is used at all. ε alone decides how many spatial components survive.
  2. WP (wavelet-packet) stage — α only. Each of the r surviving components is wavelet-packet compressed with threshold τ_k = α·σ₀/sv[k]. α alone decides how much fine temporal/high-frequency detail survives within those components.

They’re not fully independent in effect, though: τ_k is normalized by sv[k], and which singular values survive to be thresholded is exactly what ε controls — so a given α lands differently depending on ε’s choice of surviving components. This turns out to matter a lot below.

Bottom line: the shipped aggressive tier (ε=450, α=96) measurably hurts decoding — feedback especially — with no warning from RMSE. Sweeping ε or α alone barely buys any extra compression over default while still costing decoding fidelity; only scaling both together traces a real trade-off, and on it, default (ε=150, α=28) already sits close to the useful edge. Recommendation: retire the aggressive tier; keep default as standard; ε=250/α=50 is the only non-dominated fallback if more compression is ever required. A full 2D grid (next page) will refine this.

Method

Band-power envelope features (log Hilbert amplitude, delta/theta/beta/gamma, 96 channels after 4:1 spatial binning), computed identically for every compression tier from the same Cadzow-denoised checkpoint (lf_resampled_car_cadzow.npy), decoded with:

Target Feature window Decoder Metric
|wheel velocity| continuous, 50 ms bins RidgeCV, 5-fold chronological CV R²
choice [-0.2, 0) s rel. firstMovement_times Standardized LogisticRegressionCV, 5-fold stratified CV balanced accuracy
feedback [0, 0.2) s rel. feedback_times same balanced accuracy

Null: a simple per-fold label/target shuffle — not a pseudo-session control, so it understates single-recording significance, but it’s held identical across tiers, which is what matters for a relative compression-effect comparison. Sample times (t0 is nan on these benchmark files) are reconstructed via SpikeSortingLoader.timesprobe2times.

Does compression hurt decoding?

r2_wheel balanced_accuracy_choice balanced_accuracy_feedback
mean median mean median mean median
tier
uncompressed 0.139 0.134 0.564 0.546 0.642 0.568
alpha28 (default) 0.127 0.133 0.563 0.533 0.597 0.542
aggressive (eps450, alpha96, shipped) 0.104 0.084 0.552 0.509 0.557 0.508

Default tracks uncompressed closely on every target. Aggressive erodes all three, feedback most severely (mean 0.642 → 0.557), because it’s decoded from a brief post-event window — exactly the fast, phasic structure the WP stage’s per-coefficient threshold removes first (small-magnitude coefficients are discarded before large ones, and fine time-scale structure is where LFP wavelet coefficients tend to be smallest). Wheel speed, a slower band-power average, is the least affected.

Searching for an intermediate tier

Sweeping ε alone (α=28 fixed, ε ∈ 150–450) or α alone (ε=150 fixed, α ∈ 28–96) both left total file size across the 11 recordings essentially flat (0.242 GB → ~0.21 GB either way, an ~13% reduction) while feedback-decoding retention kept dropping (to 0.60/0.39 of uncompressed, chance-corrected). Neither axis alone is a usable lever. Yet at ε=450, moving α from 28→96 — the shipped aggressive tier vs. the same ε at default’s α — nearly halves the file size (0.211 GB → 0.098 GB): the ε/α interaction described above in action. Real compression only appears when both are pushed together.

r2_wheel balanced_accuracy_choice balanced_accuracy_feedback cr_realized total_GB
tier
uncompressed 0.139 0.564 0.642 1.000 20.402
alpha28 (default) 0.127 0.563 0.597 86.679 0.242
eps250/alpha50 0.117 0.552 0.575 103.736 0.201
eps350/alpha75 0.109 0.549 0.558 128.251 0.163
aggressive (eps450, alpha96, shipped) 0.104 0.552 0.557 217.478 0.098

Realized CR climbs steadily (87×→104×→128×→217×) as feedback retention falls in step (0.688→0.530→0.410→0.402) — no free knee: every step away from default costs real fidelity immediately. eps350/alpha75 is dominated by the shipped aggressive tier (almost the same feedback cost, barely half the compression) — not worth using.

Recommendation

  • Keep default (ε=150, α=28) as the standard cohort-wide tier — no tested point clears even a modest (85%) retained-decoding bar.
  • If more compression is required, use ε=250, α=50 (~104× realized, ~17% smaller than default) — a real, disclosed cost (feedback retention 0.530 vs. default’s 0.688, chance-corrected), not a free win.
  • Retire the aggressive tier (ε=450, α=96) for decoding-sensitive use. It’s a legitimate choice only if ~104× isn’t enough and the larger feedback cost of ~217× is explicitly accepted — nothing between ε=250/α=50 and aggressive is worth shipping.
  • Build command (per-recording, ≈10–60 s from the existing Cadzow checkpoint, no re-download needed): lfpack.compress_to_h5(cadzow_npy, out_h5, recording=pid, epsilon=250.0, alpha=50.0, fs=250.0, ...).

This diagonal-only search only sampled the line between two points, though. A full 2D grid across both parameters — from milder-than-default through aggressive — is in progress to properly characterize the ε/α trade-off surface.

## Overview

The [SVD/WP compression benchmark](index.qmd) calibrates ε and α against **RMSE and SNR** — a
spatial/amplitude fidelity proxy that says nothing about whether the *information* downstream
analyses use survives compression. This page checks that directly, by decoding wheel speed,
choice and feedback from LFP band-power envelopes across the 11 benchmark recordings, then uses
the result to search for a better operating point than the current two-tier design.

**lfpack's codec is two independent stages, applied in sequence** (`compress()` in
`packages/lfpack/src/lfpack/_core.py`):

1. **SVD stage — ε only.** Rank `r = #{k : sv[k] > ε·σ₀}` is fixed from the raw singular-value
   spectrum before α is used at all. ε alone decides how many spatial components survive.
2. **WP (wavelet-packet) stage — α only.** Each of the `r` surviving components is
   wavelet-packet compressed with threshold `τ_k = α·σ₀/sv[k]`. α alone decides how much fine
   temporal/high-frequency detail survives *within* those components.

They're not fully independent in effect, though: `τ_k` is normalized by `sv[k]`, and which
singular values survive to be thresholded is exactly what ε controls — so a given α lands
differently depending on ε's choice of surviving components. This turns out to matter a lot
below.

**Bottom line:** the shipped aggressive tier (ε=450, α=96) measurably hurts decoding — feedback
especially — with no warning from RMSE. Sweeping ε or α *alone* barely buys any extra
compression over default while still costing decoding fidelity; only scaling both together
traces a real trade-off, and on it, default (ε=150, α=28) already sits close to the useful
edge. **Recommendation: retire the aggressive tier; keep default as standard; ε=250/α=50 is
the only non-dominated fallback if more compression is ever required.** A full 2D grid (next
page) will refine this.

## Method

Band-power envelope features (log Hilbert amplitude, delta/theta/beta/gamma, 96 channels after
4:1 spatial binning), computed identically for every compression tier from the same
Cadzow-denoised checkpoint (`lf_resampled_car_cadzow.npy`), decoded with:

| Target | Feature window | Decoder | Metric |
|---|---|---|---|
| \|wheel velocity\| | continuous, 50 ms bins | RidgeCV, 5-fold chronological CV | R² |
| choice | [-0.2, 0) s rel. `firstMovement_times` | Standardized LogisticRegressionCV, 5-fold stratified CV | balanced accuracy |
| feedback | [0, 0.2) s rel. `feedback_times` | same | balanced accuracy |

Null: a simple per-fold label/target shuffle — not a pseudo-session control, so it understates
single-recording significance, but it's held identical across tiers, which is what matters for
a *relative* compression-effect comparison. Sample times (t0 is `nan` on these benchmark files)
are reconstructed via `SpikeSortingLoader.timesprobe2times`.

## Does compression hurt decoding?

```{python}
#| echo: false
import pandas as pd
m = pd.read_csv("2026-08-31_compression_tuning_metrics.csv")
base_order = ["uncompressed", "alpha28 (default)", "aggressive (eps450, alpha96, shipped)"]
m.groupby("tier")[["r2_wheel", "balanced_accuracy_choice", "balanced_accuracy_feedback"]].agg(["mean", "median"]).loc[base_order].round(3)
```

![Wheel-speed decoding R² per recording, vs shuffled null (black ticks).](figures/2026-08-31_lfp-compression-decoding_r2-by-pid.png){.lightbox}

![Choice / feedback balanced accuracy per recording, one box per tier. Dashed line = chance.](figures/2026-08-31_lfp-compression-decoding_categorical_boxplot.png){.lightbox}

Default tracks uncompressed closely on every target. Aggressive erodes all three, feedback most
severely (mean 0.642 → 0.557), because it's decoded from a brief post-event window — exactly
the fast, phasic structure the WP stage's per-coefficient threshold removes first (small-magnitude
coefficients are discarded before large ones, and fine time-scale structure is where LFP
wavelet coefficients tend to be smallest). Wheel speed, a slower band-power average, is the
least affected.

## Searching for an intermediate tier

Sweeping **ε alone** (α=28 fixed, ε ∈ 150–450) or **α alone** (ε=150 fixed, α ∈ 28–96) both left
total file size across the 11 recordings essentially flat (0.242 GB → ~0.21 GB either way, an
~13% reduction) while feedback-decoding retention kept dropping (to 0.60/0.39 of uncompressed,
chance-corrected). Neither axis alone is a usable lever. Yet at ε=450, moving α from 28→96 —
the shipped aggressive tier vs. the same ε at default's α — *nearly halves* the file size
(0.211 GB → 0.098 GB): the ε/α interaction described above in action. Real compression only
appears when both are pushed together.

```{python}
#| echo: false
diag_order = ["uncompressed", "alpha28 (default)", "eps250/alpha50", "eps350/alpha75",
              "aggressive (eps450, alpha96, shipped)"]
tbl = m.groupby("tier")[["r2_wheel", "balanced_accuracy_choice", "balanced_accuracy_feedback", "cr_realized"]].mean().loc[diag_order]
tbl["total_GB"] = m.groupby("tier")["file_bytes"].sum().loc[diag_order] / 1e9
tbl.round(3)
```

![Diagonal sweep (ε and α scaled together, default → shipped aggressive): wheel R², choice/feedback balanced accuracy, and total file size (realized CR labelled), 11 recordings.](figures/2026-08-31_diagonal_sweep_decoding_summary.png){.lightbox}

![Median channel-averaged PSD, diagonal sweep — cleanly ordered by compression level; the high-frequency roll-off tracks decoding cost directly.](figures/2026-08-31_diagonal_sweep_psd.png){.lightbox}

Realized CR climbs steadily (87×→104×→128×→217×) as feedback retention falls in step
(0.688→0.530→0.410→0.402) — **no free knee**: every step away from default costs real fidelity
immediately. `eps350/alpha75` is dominated by the shipped aggressive tier (almost the same
feedback cost, barely half the compression) — not worth using.

## Recommendation

- **Keep default (ε=150, α=28)** as the standard cohort-wide tier — no tested point clears even
  a modest (85%) retained-decoding bar.
- **If more compression is required, use ε=250, α=50** (~104× realized, ~17% smaller than
  default) — a real, disclosed cost (feedback retention 0.530 vs. default's 0.688,
  chance-corrected), not a free win.
- **Retire the aggressive tier (ε=450, α=96)** for decoding-sensitive use. It's a legitimate
  choice only if ~104× isn't enough and the larger feedback cost of ~217× is explicitly
  accepted — nothing between ε=250/α=50 and aggressive is worth shipping.
- **Build command** (per-recording, ≈10–60 s from the existing Cadzow checkpoint, no
  re-download needed): `lfpack.compress_to_h5(cadzow_npy, out_h5, recording=pid, epsilon=250.0,
  alpha=50.0, fs=250.0, ...)`.

This diagonal-only search only sampled the line between two points, though. A full 2D grid
across both parameters — from milder-than-default through aggressive — is in progress to
properly characterize the ε/α trade-off surface.
